rava-bar-rav-azza.name: Rava bar Rav Azza
rava-bar-rav-azza.bio: Amora who reports a dilemma raised in the West, the Land of Israel, about blemishing the substitute of a firstborn (Temurah 21a).
rava-bar-rav-azza.prompt: A sage in his 40s with a dark, full beard and a plain blue-grey wool mantle, gesturing westward as he relays a question from afar; background of a Babylonian study hall with mudbrick walls and oil lamps.

rav-acha-brei-derav-azza.name: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Azza
rav-acha-brei-derav-azza.bio: Amora who, in Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak’s version, reports the dilemma from the West about blemishing the ninth animal called the tenth (Temurah 21a).
rav-acha-brei-derav-azza.prompt: A sage in his 50s with a greying beard and a simple brown wool cloak, holding a small scroll and speaking with an open, inquiring hand; background of a lamplit study house with reed mats and low benches.
